name: Local sovereign stack
tagline: Fully agentic on your own hardware — no cloud dependency, no data leaves the desk.
audience: Privacy-first builders and tinkerers who want agents running on metal they own.

slots.why: The OS is the agent's floor: shell access, scriptability, package management.
Serves the model to every agent on the box — throughput and OpenAI-compat API matter most.
The brain. Pick by VRAM budget; coding-tuned open-weight models close most of the gap to hosted frontier models for agent loops.

pick.name: Qwen3-Coder / DeepSeek-V3.2 / Llama 4 (by VRAM budget)
pick.note: Editorial pick — models aren't an arena yet, so this slot is judgment, not judged.

slots.why: Unified memory is the local-agent bottleneck: fit the biggest model you can hold in fast memory.

pick.name: Mac Studio (128GB+ unified) or Linux box with RTX 5090 / dual 4090
pick.note: Editorial pick — hardware isn't an arena yet, so this slot is judgment, not judged.

slots.why: The hands. Point it at the local runtime's OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

name: Agentic founder stack
tagline: Run a startup where your agents do the ops: banking, planning, shipping, and listening.
audience: Founders who want every operational tool reachable by their agents, not just by hand.

slots.why: Agents that can read balances, categorize transactions, and draft payments via API/MCP.
Where agents file, triage, and update work items alongside the team.
PRs, issues, and CI an agent can drive end-to-end.
The engineering multiplier — ships against the repo above.
Agents that mine intent from user feedback and route it into the PM tool.
Agents that run payroll previews, onboard hires, and reconcile journals via API/MCP.

name: Agent builder stack
tagline: Everything an agent needs to see, fetch, run, and ship on the open web.
audience: Developers building agents that act on the world: scrape it, deploy to it, front it.

slots.why: Agents need eyes — structured extraction from any URL.
Where the agent's own services deploy and run.
The surface the agent generates UI with — docs quality and conventions agents can follow.
Builds and maintains the whole thing.
Cheap local inference for testing agent loops before burning hosted tokens.

name: Mobile agentic stack
tagline: Drive your agents and infrastructure from a phone — the pairing people actually run.
audience: Operators who want to supervise agents, repos, and servers from anywhere.

slots.why: The SSH client you live in — keys, snippets, and port forwarding on the phone.

pick.note: Curated pairing: Termius + Tailscale bind together in practice — the terminal rides the mesh network's stable IPs, so your agent boxes are reachable from anywhere without exposing ports.

slots.why: Every agent box, home server, and laptop on one flat private network.

pick.note: Curated pairing: the other half of the Termius bind — SSH targets get stable MagicDNS names; nothing is exposed to the public internet.

slots.why: Review and merge the agent's PRs from the phone.
Kick off runs remotely; check results when they land.

name: API-first team stack
tagline: Design, test, gate, and ship APIs that agents consume as first-class clients.
audience: Teams whose product is an API — and who want agents driving the whole lifecycle.

slots.why: Collections, testing, mocking, and gateway — the API team's home base.
Spec-first reviews and CI contract tests an agent can drive.
Where the API actually serves from.
Writes the handlers, keeps the OpenAPI spec honest.

name: Open-source sovereign stack
tagline: Every layer open source — auditable, self-hostable, fork-proof.
audience: Teams with a hard open-source requirement who still want maximum agent leverage.

slots.why: The best agent you can read the source of.
Autonomous end-to-end development, self-hosted.
Open weights on open serving.
Your repos on your metal.
Open extraction for agent eyes.
Git-native, offline API workflows.

name: Financial ops stack
tagline: The founder money stack: bank, get paid, pay people, close the books — all agent-reachable.
audience: Founders and finance leads who want agents doing the monthly grind.

slots.why: Balances, transactions, and payment drafting via API/MCP.
Charging customers — the deepest API surface in the stack (Stripe et al).
Tap-to-pay and terminal fleets driven by API.
Payroll previews, onboarding, and journal reconciliation by agent.
The ledger agents close against — API depth decides everything here.

name: Regulated fintech stack
tagline: Money movement with auditors in the room: banking, payments, ledger, and code security that survive a compliance review.
audience: Fintech teams building under regulatory scrutiny — where every flow needs an audit trail and every repo needs scanning.

slots.why: The operating account — statements, controls, and API access an auditor and an agent can both follow.
Card acceptance with the dispute, fraud, and reconciliation depth regulators expect.
The system of record — the ledger everything above must reconcile into, cleanly and programmatically.
Secret detection and dependency scanning in CI — table stakes before any fintech audit.

name: Indie hacker stack
tagline: Ship a real product on a ramen budget: open source where it protects you, free tiers where it doesn't.
audience: Solo builders shipping side projects that might become the main thing — minimal lock-in, minimal invoice.

slots.why: Database, auth, and storage in one — open source so the backend can move to your own box when the bill matters.
The UI layer — pick the framework agents and docs serve best, not the one with the loudest fans.
Deploy on the platform whose free/hobby path goes furthest before a card is required.
Know if anyone showed up — open source and self-hostable, so insight never becomes a subscription hostage.

name: Support & GTM stack
tagline: Close the loop from lead to feedback: CRM, analytics, chat, and intent capture your agents can work end-to-end.
audience: Founders and ops leads running go-to-market where agents enrich records, mine feedback, and route it to the team.

What users actually do — funnels and retention agents can query for the GTM story.
Where the loop closes — bots post the signal into the room where humans decide.
Capture what users ask for and turn it into prioritized, buildable work.

name: Incorporation-day stack
tagline: The day-one founder set — bank, payroll, books, tracker, repo — the tool half of an ultrametric.ai/process incorporation checklist.

The shared brain for what's next — where founders and agents file and triage the same work.
The company's first repo — PRs, CI, and issues agents can drive from commit zero.

name: gstack (Garry Tan)
tagline: Garry Tan's (Y Combinator CEO) published AI-coding setup — the judged-product half of github.com/garrytan/gstack, as of 2026-09-28 — every scored slot below resolves from our own arena evidence, not his.
audience: Builders adopting the most famous solo-founder workflow in startups: one person running an AI engineering team.

slots.why: The host gstack lives in — all 23 skills are slash commands inside it.

pick.note: gstack's required foundation per its README: every skill runs as a Claude Code command. The repo ships adapters for other agents (Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode…), but Claude Code is the canonical host.

slots.why: gstack's power tools and scripts execute under Bun (v1.0+ is a hard requirement).

pick.note: Listed as a required prerequisite in the gstack README alongside Claude Code and Git — the tooling layer everything else runs on.

slots.why: GBrain, gstack's persistent knowledge base, stores to Supabase when cloud-hosted.

pick.note: Named in the gstack README as the storage for hosted GBrain instances and optional telemetry; local-only setups use PGLite instead (not judged here).

slots.why: Remote agent coordination across machines — the multi-box half of the workflow.

pick.note: Named in the gstack README for coordinating agents across machines — the same mesh pattern our Mobile agentic stack curates with Termius.

slots.why: The 23 skills and 8 power tools — the part of gstack that is the setup, not a judged product.

pick.name: gstack (github.com/garrytan/gstack)
pick.note: Source of record for this stack, verified live 2026-09-28 (repo created 2026-03-11, MIT, ~134k stars; no versioned releases — main is canonical). Honest gaps — gstack members no arena judges yet, so they carry no score here: Git (the VCS itself), Node.js (Windows-only prereq), the Aside browser, Playwright, PGLite, and gstack's own mods (GBrain, impeccable, OpenClaw).
